extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent applicants and practitioners seeking to use the USPTO Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) program
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/procedure rules for obtaining accelerated examination under the USPTO Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) based on an Office of Earlier Examination (OEE) work product. Covers required documents, claim-correspondence rules, timing, translations, and program-specific processing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is PPH and how does it help me?
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) is a framework in which an application whose claims have been determined to be patentable by an Office of Earlier Examination (OEE) is eligible to go through an accelerated examination in an Office of Later Examination (OLE) with a simple procedure upon an applicant’s request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH uses search/examination-related information of the OEE to (1) deliver lower prosecution costs, (2) support efficient worldwide patent rights, and (3) reduce search/examination burden and improve examination quality among major patent offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where can I obtain a complete listing of PPH participating Offices?
rubrics_metrics.description: The complete list of Offices participating with the USPTO in the PPH is available at the USPTO PPH web page and via the JPO one-stop PPH portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: URLs provided: http://www.uspto.gov/patents/init_events/pph/index.jsp and JPO portal (http://www.jpo.go.jp/ppph-portal/index.htm) for up-to-date program info, statistics, and forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: How do I know if my USPTO patent application is eligible for PPH?
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility requires: (1) common earliest priority date with a related application from a partnering PPH office; (2) an indication of allowability for at least one claim in the related application; (3) all claims in the USPTO application sufficiently correspond to allowable claims in the related application; and (4) substantive examination has not begun on the USPTO application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Question 27 for sufficient correspondence details and Question 30 for definition of examination begun.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is an application filed before the starting date of the PPH program eligible?
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes, applications filed before the PPH program start date can participate provided they meet the other eligibility criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are any types of applications excluded from the PPH program?
rubrics_metrics.description: Excluded application types: provisional applications, plant applications, design applications, reissue applications, reexamination proceedings, and applications subject to a secrecy order.

rubrics_metrics.name: How do I participate in the PPH program at the USPTO?
rubrics_metrics.description: To have your application considered you must meet all eligibility criteria and submit via EFS-Web a PPH Request form along with supporting documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A list of PPH Request forms is available on the USPTO PPH web page.

rubrics_metrics.name: What supporting documents need to be submitted with the PPH Request form?
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must submit the PPH Request form, a copy of the appropriate OEE work product (with English translation if applicable), and an Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) listing references cited in the OEE work product along with copies of non-U.S. patent references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the OEE work product is already present in the USPTO application or available via the Dossier Access System or PATENTSCOPE, a separate copy need not be supplied. Any IDS or reference copies already in your USPTO application need not be resubmitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Can a PPH request be filed if the executed declaration of the inventors has not yet been filed?
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes. An executed declaration of the inventors is not a supporting document required with a PPH request.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFS-Web document description for submitting PPH
rubrics_metrics.description: The document description for the PPH request is 'Petition to make special under Patent Pros Hwy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the IDS use 'Information Disclosure Statement (IDS).' For a preliminary amendment accompanying the PPH request use 'Preliminary amendment.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Which OEE office action must be furnished as the OEE work product?
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OEE application is not a PCT application, provide a copy of the office action immediately prior to the 'Decision to Grant a Patent.' If the OEE application is a PCT application, provide the latest PCT work product (e.g., Written Opinion of the ISA, Written Opinion of the IPEA, or International Preliminary Examination Report).

rubrics_metrics.name: How can applicant determine whether an OEE office action is available via the Dossier Access System?
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant can check the Dossier Access System web site and the WIPO PATENTSCOPE to determine availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In some cases dossiers are accessible only to IP offices. If unsure or unable to determine availability, provide a copy of the OEE work product to avoid dismissal of the PPH request. Verify availability before requesting USPTO retrieval via Dossier Access System or PATENTSCOPE.

rubrics_metrics.name: If an English translation of the OEE work product is required, what translations are acceptable?
rubrics_metrics.description: The English translation may be a machine translation. If the USPTO finds it of such poor quality that it is difficult to understand, the applicant may be required to submit a manual translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A manual translation does not need to be certified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Can I rely on allowed claims from a utility model or an innovation patent from an OEE?
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally no — utility models and innovation patents typically are not subjected to substantive examination and do not meet the same patentability standards as regular utility patents. Exception: Korean utility models (see USPTO notice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO may consider practices in other countries for future inclusion but no decisions made at this time.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is an Extended European Search Report (EESR) and when may it be relied upon?
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO generates an EESR prior to an office action. If the EESR only contains 'A' references (no 'X' or 'Y' references) directed to a particular claim, that claim is considered allowable by the EPO and may be used as the basis for a PPH request in the U.S. application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Should I submit an IDS listing references cited in an OEE Decision to Grant even if there was no rejection?
rubrics_metrics.description: Although not an explicit PPH requirement, the applicant has a duty to bring to the attention of the Office any material prior art or other information cited or brought to applicant's attention in any related foreign application (see MPEP 2001.06(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: When documents cited in an IDS are in a foreign language, are English translations required?
rubrics_metrics.description: The IDS must comply with 37 CFR 1.98. If documents are not in English, submit a concise explanation of relevance pursuant to 37 CFR 1.98(a)(3). If the document was cited in a foreign search report, the requirement can be satisfied by submitting an English-language version of the search report or action indicating relevance (see MPEP 609.04(a), subsection III).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing a PPH request with a U.S. national stage (35 U.S.C. 371) entry
rubrics_metrics.description: You may file your PPH request with national stage entry papers or at any time prior to the start of substantive examination. If you have not received the U.S. national stage application number, you may indicate 'filed herewith' or 'TBD' on the PPH Request form. The filing date of a U.S. national stage application is the international filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 35 U.S.C. 363 and MPEP 1893.03(b) for filing date rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical processing time for a PPH request
rubrics_metrics.description: Information regarding processing time can be found on the Petitions Timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: How will I know if my PPH request is granted?
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will send a decision on the request for participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Can I amend errors in a PPH request before decision?
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have not received a decision, submit a corrected PPH request via EFS-Web as soon as possible and include a transmittal letter explaining the corrections. If you have received a decision, submit the corrected PPH request in your reply to the PPH decision with a transmittal letter explaining the errors being corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time period for filing a renewed PPH request after dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is given ONE opportunity within ONE MONTH from the mailing date of dismissal to perfect (correct noted deficiencies) a renewed request for participation. No extension under 37 CFR 1.136 is permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If deficiencies are not corrected within the given time, the application will await action in its regular turn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Can I file a new PPH request after a renewed PPH request was denied?
rubrics_metrics.description: No. If the PPH request is denied (as opposed to dismissed), applicant may not file a new or renewed PPH request in the same application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A PPH request may, however, be filed in a continuing application.

rubrics_metrics.name: How much quicker will an application proceed if PPH is filed?
rubrics_metrics.description: PPH does not have the AE program's 12-month final disposition goal, does not require filing at time of application, and does not expedite pre-exam processing. Generally, if PPH request is granted and pre-exam processing is complete, the examiner will examine the application within 2 to 3 months from grant of the PPH request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is withdrawal from the PPH program possible after grant?
rubrics_metrics.description: No. Once a PPH request is granted, the application is accorded special status which is retained throughout prosecution of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If participation is no longer desired, applicant may consider filing a continuing application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does PPH special status apply to continuing applications?
rubrics_metrics.description: No. Special status under PPH does not carry over to a continuing application (continuation, continuation-in-part, or divisional).

rubrics_metrics.name: If an RCE is filed after PPH grant, will the PPH status still apply?
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes. Filing an RCE continues prosecution in the same application, and the application retains its special PPH status throughout prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: How is sufficient correspondence between claims determined?
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim sufficiently corresponds when it is of the same or similar scope as an allowable claim in the related OEE application. A claim that is narrower than an allowable OEE claim will also sufficiently correspond if presented as a claim dependent upon a claim that is of the same or similar scope to an allowable OEE claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Questions 28–29 and 34–35 for category and amendment constraints and acceptable dependent-to-independent conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Can I include corresponding apparatus claims if OEE allowed only method claims?
rubrics_metrics.description: No. Introducing a different category of claims (e.g., apparatus when OEE allowed only method claims) is not considered to sufficiently correspond, even if presented as dependent upon a corresponding claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Can 'use' claims be rewritten as 'method' claims when filing a PPH request?
rubrics_metrics.description: No. Presenting a 'method' claim where the OEE allowed a 'use' claim introduces a different claim category and is not considered to sufficiently correspond. The scopes of 'use' and 'method' claims usually differ significantly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does 'examination has not begun' mean substantive examination?
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes. The requirement refers to substantive examination. Formalities review (e.g., Notice to File Missing Parts) is not substantive examination. A restriction requirement does not count as start of substantive examination if the examiner has not started on the first action on the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Will a PPH-eligible application be granted without substantive examination?
rubrics_metrics.description: No. Substantive examination under the PPH is conducted according to U.S. law and guidelines in the same way as non-PPH applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not guaranteed to match the OEE result, PPH applications generally have higher allowance rates, fewer office actions per disposal, reduced RCE filing rates, and reduced appeal rates than non-PPH applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: If I received an office action on the merits after filing PPH but before decision, is my application eligible?
rubrics_metrics.description: No. If substantive examination (first office action on the merits) began before the PPH request is granted, the application is not eligible and the PPH request will be denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Can a new U.S. continuation/divisional application be eligible for PPH if the parent received a first office action?
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes. A newly filed U.S. continuation or divisional application may be eligible to participate in PPH based on allowable claims from the OEE application even if the original U.S. application has already received a first office action on the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporating a narrower dependent claim into the independent claim during U.S. prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: If the narrower dependent claim is indicated as being allowable if written in independent form, you may rewrite the allowable dependent claim in independent form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This addresses whether dependent-to-independent conversion is permissible when dependent claim was indicated allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Will an amendment to an independent claim meet sufficient correspondence if it adds a limitation?
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes, but only if the added limitation was previously presented in a dependent claim that is indicated as having allowable subject matter but was objected to only because it was dependent on a rejected base claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does Patent Term Adjustment (PTA) apply to PPH applications?
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes. PTA still applies to applications accepted in the PPH program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) available for PPH applications?
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes. Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are available during prosecution of U.S. applications accepted in the PPH program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Can an applicant request a written restriction letter in a PPH application?
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes. MPEP 708.02(a), section III describes telephonic restriction practice for applications made special; however, applications made special for health/age and PPH are not subject to that telephonic restriction requirement, so it is permissible to request a written restriction letter in a PPH application.
